title: Full mock 1
description: Original full-length mock. Sections 1–2 follow the TU Delft CST (Mathematics; Systematic Reasoning & Logical Thinking); section 3 adds the TU/e Algorithmic Thinking test.

questions.prompt: Solve for $x$: $5x - 7 = 2x + 8$.
questions.hint: Collect the x-terms on one side.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 5*x-7-(2*x+8); const r=h.roots(f,-50.3,50).map(x=> Math.round(x*1e9)/1e9); if(r.length!==1) throw new Error("expected one root, got "+r); return r[0];

questions.prompt: $f(x) = x^3 - 2x$. Compute $f'(2)$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> x**3-2*x; return h.deriv(f,2);

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^2 3x^2\,dx$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 3*x*x; return h.integrate(f,0,2);

questions.prompt: Compute $\log_5 125$.

verifier.code: return Math.log(125)/Math.log(5);

questions.prompt: What is $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$?

verifier.code: const v=Math.cos(Math.PI/3); const vals=[0.5,Math.sqrt(3)/2,Math.sqrt(2)/2,0]; const d=vals.map(x=> Math.abs(x-v)); const i=d.indexOf(Math.min(...d)); if(d[i]>1e-6*Math.max(1,Math.abs(v))) throw new Error("no option matches "+v); return {index:i};

questions.prompt: What is the distance between $(-1, 1)$ and $(5, 9)$?

verifier.code: return Math.hypot(5-(-1), 9-1);

questions.prompt: How many integers $x$ satisfy $|x + 1| < 3$?
questions.explanation: $-3 < x + 1 < 3 \iff -4 < x < 2$: the integers $-3, -2, -1, 0, 1$. That is 5.

verifier.code: return h.range(-100,100).filter(x=> Math.abs(x+1)<3).length;

questions.prompt: $f(x) = x^2 - 1$ and $g(x) = 2x + 3$. Compute $f(g(-1))$.

verifier.code: const f=x=> x*x-1, g=x=> 2*x+3; return f(g(-1));

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 2} \frac{x^2-4}{x-2}$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> (x*x-4)/(x-2); return h.limit(f,2);
const f=(x)=> (x*x+1)**3; return h.deriv(f,1);

questions.prompt: What is the maximum value of $f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + 1$?

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> -x*x+4*x+1; const a=(-20), b=(20); let best=f(a); for(let i=1;i<=400000;i++) best=Math.max(best, f(a+(b-a)*i/400000)); return best;

questions.prompt: $s(t) = t^3 - 3t^2$. What is the acceleration at $t = 2$?

verifier.code: return h.deriv2(t=> t**3-3*t*t, 2);

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^1 (4x^3 + 2x)\,dx$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 4*x**3+2*x; return h.integrate(f,0,1);

questions.prompt: What is the area between the graph of $y = 4 - x^2$ and the $x$-axis? Give an exact fraction.
questions.hint: Find where the graph meets the axis.

verifier.code: const r=h.roots(x=> 4-x*x, -10.3, 10); return h.integrate(x=> 4-x*x, r[0], r[1]);

questions.prompt: Solve $9^x = 27$.
questions.hint: Write both sides as powers of 3.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> 9**x-27; const r=h.roots(f,-10.3,10).map(x=> Math.round(x*1e9)/1e9); if(r.length!==1) throw new Error("expected one root, got "+r); return r[0];

questions.prompt: The point $(1, 2)$ lies on the curve $xy + y^2 = 6$. Find $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ there.

verifier.code: const Y=x=> h.root(y=> x*y+y*y-6, 1.5, 2.5); return h.deriv(Y, 1, 1e-3);

questions.prompt: A farmer has 100 m of fence to enclose a rectangle against a long wall (the wall forms one side, so only three sides need fence). What is the largest area (in m²)?
questions.hint: Let x be the length of each side perpendicular to the wall.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> x*(100-2*x); const a=(0), b=(50); let best=f(a); for(let i=1;i<=400000;i++) best=Math.max(best, f(a+(b-a)*i/400000)); return best;

questions.prompt: Compute $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin x\cos x\,dx$.

verifier.code: const f=(x)=> Math.sin(x)*Math.cos(x); return h.integrate(f,0,Math.PI/2);

questions.prompt: How many solutions does $2\cos x = 1$ have in $[0, 4\pi)$?
questions.hint: Find the solutions in one period first.
questions.explanation: $\cos x = \frac12$ gives $x = \frac\pi3$ and $\frac{5\pi}3$ in $[0, 2\pi)$, and the same plus $2\pi$ in the second period: 4 solutions.

verifier.code: return h.roots(x=> 2*Math.cos(x)-1, 0, 4*Math.PI-1e-9).length;

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides 7, 8 and 13. How many degrees is the angle opposite the side of length 13?
questions.hint: Cosine rule, solved for the angle.

verifier.code: const a=7,b=8,c=13; const x=(a*a+c*c-b*b)/(2*c); const y=Math.sqrt(a*a-x*x); const P=[0,0],Q=[c,0],R=[x,y]; const v1=[P[0]-R[0],P[1]-R[1]], v2=[Q[0]-R[0],Q[1]-R[1]]; return Math.acos((v1[0]*v2[0]+v1[1]*v2[1])/(Math.hypot(...v1)*Math.hypot(...v2)))*180/Math.PI;

questions.prompt: p is false and q is true. What is the value of p ∨ ¬q?
questions.explanation: ¬q is false and p is false, so p ∨ ¬q is false.

questions.prompt: In how many of the 8 rows is p ∧ (q ∨ r) true?
questions.explanation: p must be true (4 rows) and q ∨ r true (3 of the 4 combinations): 3 rows.

questions.prompt: Which formula is equivalent to ¬(p ∨ ¬q)?
Which statement is equivalent to ¬∃x (P(x) ∧ Q(x))?
questions.hint: Push the negation inside and use ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ A → ¬B.

verifier.code: const D=[0,1,2]; const un=[]; for(let m=0;m<8;m++) un.push(x=>((m>>x)&1)===1); const all=f=>D.every(f), ex=f=>D.some(f); const t=(P,Q)=> !ex(x=> P(x)&&Q(x)); const o=[(P,Q)=> all(x=> !P(x)||!Q(x)), (P,Q)=> ex(x=> P(x)&&!Q(x)), (P,Q)=> all(x=> !P(x)&&!Q(x)), (P,Q)=> ex(x=> !(P(x)||Q(x)))]; return {indices: o.flatMap((g,i)=> un.every(P=> un.every(Q=> g(P,Q)===t(P,Q)))?[i]:[])};

questions.prompt: "If the shop is open, the lights are on. The lights are off. Therefore the shop is closed." Is this argument valid?
questions.explanation: This is modus tollens (o → l, ¬l ⊢ ¬o): valid.

questions.prompt: "q is necessary for p." Which formula expresses this?
questions.hint: If q is necessary, p cannot happen without q.
questions.explanation: A necessary condition must hold whenever p does: p → q.

questions.prompt: a = "Ann came", b = "Bob came". Which formula expresses "Neither Ann nor Bob came"?
In how many of the 8 rows is (p → q) ∨ (q → r) **false**?
questions.explanation: (p → q) ∨ (q → r) ≡ ¬p ∨ q ∨ ¬q ∨ r, which contains q ∨ ¬q: it is a tautology. 0 false rows.

questions.prompt: Simplify (p ∨ q) ∧ ¬p.
Select **all** formulas equivalent to ¬(p ∧ q).
questions.explanation: ¬p ∨ ¬q (De Morgan), p → ¬q and q → ¬p (both ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q), and ¬(q ∧ p) (commutativity). ¬p ∧ ¬q is stronger.

questions.prompt: The domain is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Select **all** true statements.
questions.hint: Check each against the five elements.
questions.explanation: ∀x (x < 6): true. ∃x (x² = 10): false. ∀x ∃y (y > x): false for x = 5. ∃x ∀y (x ≤ y): x = 1 — true. ∃x (x is even ∧ x is prime): x = 2 — true.

verifier.code: const D=h.range(1,5); const all=f=>D.every(f), ex=f=>D.some(f); return [all(x=>x<6), ex(x=>x*x===10), all(x=>ex(y=>y>x)), ex(x=>all(y=>x<=y)), ex(x=> x%2===0 && h.isPrime(x))];

questions.prompt: S(x): "x is a student", M(x, y): "y mentors x". Translate "Every student has a mentor."
questions.hint: Who varies with whom? Each student may have a different mentor.
questions.explanation: For every x that is a student there is some y mentoring x: ∀x (S(x) → ∃y M(x, y)). The second option claims one mentor for all students.

verifier.code: const D=[0,1,2]; const all=f=>D.every(f), ex=f=>D.some(f); const target=(S,M)=> D.filter(S).every(x=> D.some(y=> M(x,y))); const o=[(S,M)=> all(x=> !S(x) || ex(y=> M(x,y))), (S,M)=> ex(y=> all(x=> !S(x)||M(x,y))), (S,M)=> all(x=> ex(y=> S(x)&&M(x,y))), (S,M)=> ex(x=> S(x)&&all(y=>M(x,y)))]; const ok=[true,true,true,true]; for(let s=0;s<8;s++) for(let m=0;m<512;m++){ const S=x=>((s>>x)&1)===1, M=(x,y)=>((m>>(3*x+y))&1)===1; const t=target(S,M); o.forEach((g,i)=>{ if(g(S,M)!==t) ok[i]=false; }); } return {indices: ok.flatMap((v,i)=>v?[i]:[])};

questions.prompt: Is this argument valid? "All C are D. No D are E. Therefore no C are E."
questions.hint: C lies inside D; where is E?
questions.explanation: C lies inside D and D does not overlap E, so C cannot overlap E. Valid.

verifier.code: const N=4; const sets=[]; for(let m=0;m<(1<<N);m++) sets.push(Array.from({length:N},(_,i)=>((m>>i)&1)===1)); const S={all:(X,Y)=>X.every((x,i)=>!x||Y[i]), some:(X,Y)=>X.some((x,i)=>x&&Y[i]), no:(X,Y)=>X.every((x,i)=>!(x&&Y[i])), someNot:(X,Y)=>X.some((x,i)=>x&&!Y[i])}; const models=(k)=> h.tuples(sets,k);const ok=models(3).every(([A,B,C,D])=> !(S.all(A,B) && S.no(B,C)) || (S.no(A,C))); return {index: ok ? 0 : 1};

questions.prompt: From p ∨ q, q → r and ¬r, what follows?
questions.hint: Start with the last two premises.
questions.explanation: q → r and ¬r give ¬q (modus tollens). With p ∨ q this gives p.

questions.prompt: Knights always tell the truth; knaves always lie. A says: "B is a knight and I am a knave." What are A and B?
options: A is a knave, B is a knight
A is a knight, B is a knave
questions.hint: Can a knight claim to be a knave?
questions.explanation: A cannot be a knight (the claim "I am a knave" would be false). So A is a knave and the whole claim is false. Since "I am a knave" is true, "B is a knight" must be false: B is a knave too.

verifier.code: const sols=h.tuples([true,false],2).filter(k=> [k=> k[1] && !k[0],k=> k[1]].every((s,i)=> s(k)===k[i])); const desc=(k)=> k[0]&&k[1]?"Both are knights":k[0]?"A is a knight, B is a knave":k[1]?"A is a knave, B is a knight":"Both are knaves"; const got=[...new Set(sols.map(desc))]; if(got.length!==1) throw new Error("puzzle has "+sols.length+" solutions"); return got[0];

questions.prompt: In how many of the 8 rows is (p ⊕ q) ∧ (q ⊕ r) true?
questions.hint: Both exclusive ors must be true: what does that say about p and r?
questions.explanation: p ≠ q and q ≠ r, so p = r and q is the opposite: (T, F, T) or (F, T, F). 2 rows.

questions.prompt: Simplify (p → q) ∧ (p → ¬q) as far as possible and type the result.
questions.hint: Combine the two implications that share the premise p.

verifier.code: const F="(p → q) ∧ (p → ¬q)"; const c=["p","q","r","¬p","¬q","¬r","true","false","p ∧ q","p ∨ q","¬p ∧ q","p ∧ ¬q"]; return c.find(x=>h.logic.equivalent(F,x)) ?? "none";

questions.prompt: There are 16 relations R on {a, b} (subsets of {a, b} × {a, b}). For how many is ∃y ∀x R(x, y) true?
questions.hint: ∃y ∀x R(x, y) means some element is related **from** both a and b.
questions.explanation: y = a needs (a, a) and (b, a): 2² = 4 relations. y = b similarly 4. Both: 1. Inclusion–exclusion: 4 + 4 − 1 = 7.

verifier.code: let n=0; for(let m=0;m<16;m++){ const R=(x,y)=>((m>>(2*x+y))&1)===1; if([0,1].some(y=>[0,1].every(x=>R(x,y)))) n++; } return n;

questions.prompt: Select **all** valid arguments.
options: p → q, r → q, q ⊢ p ∨ r
questions.hint: Look for a counterexample row for each.
questions.explanation: 1: two applications of modus tollens — valid. 2: disjunctive syllogism — valid. 3: q could hold for another reason — invalid. 4: ¬r gives ¬(p ∧ q) — valid. 5: p ↔ q and ¬p give ¬q — valid.

questions.prompt: Five people A, B, C, D and E sit in seats 1–5. C sits in seat 3. B sits at one of the ends. A does not sit next to B. D sits somewhere to the left of E. How many seatings are possible?
questions.explanation: If B is in seat 1, A must take seat 4 or 5, and D, E fill the rest in the one allowed order: 2 seatings. By symmetry B in seat 5 also gives 2. Total 4.

verifier.code: return h.permutations(["A","B","C","D","E"]).filter(o=>{const i=x=>o.indexOf(x); return o[2]==="C" && (i("B")===0||i("B")===4) && Math.abs(i("A")-i("B"))!==1 && i("D")<i("E");}).length;

questions.prompt: What number comes next? 5, 11, 17, 23, …

verifier.code: const s=[5,11,17,23]; const d=s[1]-s[0]; if(!s.every((x,i)=>i===0||x-s[i-1]===d)) throw new Error("x"); return s[3]+d;

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
s ← 1
for i from 1 to 4
  s ← s · 2
print s

questions.prompt: A tree has 15 nodes. How many edges does it have?
questions.hint: Trees have one edge fewer than nodes.

verifier.code: const E=h.range(2,15).map(i=> i+"-"+(i>>1)); if(Object.keys(h.bfsDist(h.graph(E),"1")).length!==15) throw new Error("x"); return E.length;

questions.prompt: Binary search on a sorted list of 100 elements: what is the maximum number of elements inspected?

verifier.code: const W=n=> n===0 ? 0 : 1 + W(Math.ceil((n-1)/2)); return W(100);

questions.prompt: What is the binary number 11010 in decimal?
questions.hint: Add the place values of the 1-bits.

verifier.code: return parseInt("11010",2);

questions.prompt: A club of 5 people chooses a president and a (different) secretary. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.hint: Order matters: the two roles are different.
questions.explanation: 5 choices for president, then 4 for secretary: 20.

verifier.code: return h.tuples(h.range(1,5),2).filter(([a,b])=> a!==b).length;

questions.prompt: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, …

verifier.code: const s=[2,3,5,8,12,17]; const d=s.slice(1).map((x,i)=>x-s[i]); if(!d.every((x,i)=> i===0||x===d[i-1]+1)) throw new Error("x"); return s[5]+d[4]+1;

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
n ← 100
c ← 0
while n ≥ 1
  n ← n div 3
  c ← c + 1
print c
questions.hint: Keep a table of n and c.
questions.explanation: n: 100 → 33 → 11 → 3 → 1 → 0. The loop body ran 5 times, so c = 5.

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
questions.code:
A ← [2, 7, 1, 8, 2, 8]
c ← 0
for i from 1 to 6
  if A[i] > 3 then
    c ← c + A[i]
print c
questions.hint: Only elements larger than 3 are added.

questions.prompt: Roads and their lengths are listed. What is the length of the shortest route from A to E?
questions.code:
A — B : 2
A — C : 6
B — C : 3
B — D : 8
C — D : 2
D — E : 1
C — E : 7
questions.hint: Fix the closest town first, repeatedly.
questions.explanation: A–B (2), B–C (3), C–D (2), D–E (1): total 8. Every other route is longer (e.g. A–C–E = 13).

questions.prompt: The arrows are one-way streets. How many different routes lead from S to T?
questions.code:
S → A
S → B
A → B
A → C
B → C
B → T
C → T
questions.hint: Count the ways to reach each node.
questions.explanation: S→A→B→C→T, S→A→B→T, S→A→C→T, S→B→C→T, S→B→T: 5 routes.

verifier.code: return h.countPaths(["S>A","S>B","A>B","A>C","B>C","B>T","C>T"],"S","T");

questions.prompt: How many swaps does bubble sort make to sort [4, 3, 1, 2]?
questions.hint: Count the pairs in the wrong order.

verifier.code: const A=[4,3,1,2]; let s=0; for(let p=1;p<A.length;p++) for(let i=0;i<A.length-p;i++) if(A[i]>A[i+1]){ [A[i],A[i+1]]=[A[i+1],A[i]]; s++; } return s;

questions.prompt: A committee of 3 is chosen from 6 people, and Anna must be on it. How many committees are possible?
questions.hint: Anna's seat is fixed; choose the rest.
questions.explanation: Choose the other 2 members from the remaining 5: C(5, 2) = 10.

verifier.code: return h.combinations(h.range(1,6),3).filter(c=> c.includes(1)).length;

questions.prompt: A machine starts in X; Z is the only accepting state. How many bit strings of length 4 does it accept?
questions.code:
state | on 0 | on 1
  X   |  Y   |  X
  Y   |  Z   |  X
  Z   |  Z   |  Z
questions.hint: Find out what kind of string ends in Z.
questions.explanation: The machine reaches Z exactly when it reads two 0s in a row, and then stays there. Length-4 strings without "00": 8 (Fibonacci). So 16 − 8 = 8 are accepted.

verifier.code: const T={X:["Y","X"],Y:["Z","X"],Z:["Z","Z"]}; return h.tuples([0,1],4).filter(t=> t.reduce((s,b)=> T[s][b],"X")==="Z").length;

questions.prompt: What value is printed?
What value is printed?
questions.code:
c ← 0
for i from 1 to 5
  for j from i to 5
    if (i + j) mod 2 = 0 then
      c ← c + 1
print c
questions.explanation: i + j is even when i and j have the same parity. Odd values {1, 3, 5}: 6 pairs with i ≤ j. Even values {2, 4}: 3 pairs. Total 9.

questions.prompt: Connect all towns A–E with cables along the listed connections, using minimum total length. What is that length?
questions.code:
A — B : 3
A — C : 1
B — C : 4
B — D : 2
C — D : 5
C — E : 6
D — E : 7
questions.hint: Kruskal: cheapest edge that does not close a cycle.
questions.explanation: A–C (1), B–D (2), A–B (3); B–C (4) and C–D (5) would close cycles; C–E (6). Total 1 + 2 + 3 + 6 = 12.

questions.prompt: C is a one-element counter array (passed by reference). What value is printed?
questions.code:
function g(n, C)
  C[1] ← C[1] + 1
  if n ≤ 1 then return 1
  return g(n div 2, C) + g(n div 2, C)
C ← [0]
x ← g(8, C)
print C[1]

questions.prompt: A robot walks from (0, 0) to (3, 3) with unit steps right or up. The point (1, 1) is blocked. How many routes are possible?

verifier.code: const W={}; const f=(x,y)=>{ if(x===1&&y===1) return 0; if(x===0&&y===0) return 1; if(x<0||y<0) return 0; return W[x+","+y] ??= f(x-1,y)+f(x,y-1); }; return f(3,3);

questions.prompt: Start with the word B. In every step, every A becomes AB and every B becomes A (simultaneously). How many letters does the word have after 6 steps?
questions.explanation: Words: B, A, AB, ABA, ABAAB, … Lengths 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13: after 6 steps the word has 13 letters.

verifier.code: const R={A:"AB",B:"A"}; let w="B"; for(let i=0;i<6;i++) w=w.split("").map(c=>R[c]).join(""); return w.length;
